# Confirm the browser assistant never submits across real application pages

## What & Why
The current shared policy and cockpit coverage prove the safety rules, but the unpacked MV3 package still needs a Chromium-level harness against a synthetic multi-page application. This protects the highest-risk promise: fill only after explicit confirmation and never trigger site navigation.

## Done looks like
- Load browser/application-assist in a controlled Chromium test context
- Exercise one-shot fill, manual page advance, same-origin re-scan, undo, pause, and emergency stop
- Assert user-edited fields, passwords, uploads, sensitive questions, and Next/Continue/Submit controls remain untouched
- Assert the exported session status preserves page history after the popup is reopened

## Relevant files
- browser/application-assist/content.js
- browser/application-assist/popup.js
- browser/application-assist/manifest.json
- artifacts/escape-hatch/tests/assist.spec.ts
